tasks.title: R5: test that Dungeon.LastModified is unchanged when an inner floor mutation returns NotFound
acceptance: RemoveArea: a test in the new file DungeonLastModifiedOnFailedMutationTests.cs works on a dungeon with one existing floor. It captures `dungeon.LastModified`, waits until the clock has advanced past the captured value, and calls `RemoveArea` with that floor's id and an area id that does not exist. It asserts that the outcome is `MutationOutcome.NotFound` and that `LastModified` equals the captured value. Injection: replace the statements of TouchOnSuccess (signature at fd429e3 DungeonMethods.cs:460, statements at :462-469) with `Touch(); return outcome;`. The method returns the real outcome, so only the timestamp changes. Under the injection this test turns red, and the failing assertion is the LastModified one, not the outcome one.

UpdateArea: a test of the same shape, with an existing floor and a missing area id, asserts the outcome is `NotFound` and `LastModified` is unchanged. It turns red under the same TouchOnSuccess injection, failing on the LastModified assertion.

UpdateAreaOutline: a test of the same shape, with an existing floor, a missing area id and a valid three-segment outline, asserts the outcome is `NotFound` and `LastModified` is unchanged. It turns red under the same injection, failing on the LastModified assertion.

RemovePlacedObject: a test of the same shape, with an existing floor and a missing object id, asserts the outcome is `NotFound` and `LastModified` is unchanged. It turns red under the same injection, failing on the LastModified assertion.

UpdatePlacedObject: a test of the same shape, with an existing floor, a missing object id and otherwise valid arguments, asserts the outcome is `NotFound` and `LastModified` is unchanged. It turns red under the same injection, failing on the LastModified assertion.

Control: a success-path test in the same file uses the same capture and wait, then mutates an existing area or object through one of the five facade methods, and asserts that the outcome is `Success` and that `LastModified` is strictly greater than the captured value. It passes on the unmodified code and stays green under the TouchOnSuccess injection. That shows the wait lets a Touch be observed, so the five unchanged-assertions cannot pass merely because the clock did not move.

No test in the new file calls `Task.Delay` or `Thread.Sleep`. The wait between capture and act is a condition wait with a timeout, for example `SpinWait.SpinUntil(() => DateTime.UtcNow > captured, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1))`, and the test asserts the wait returned true so that a timeout fails the test. This follows test discipline, Determinism: 'No sleeping. Wait on the condition, with a timeout.' It supersedes the spec's Task.Delay assumption row and the EntityEqualityTests.cs:175 precedent.

DungeonMethods.cs is owned only to host the injection, and it ends the task byte-identical to fd429e3. The report quotes PowerShell `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` for the file before the first injection and after the revert, and the two are equal.
